name: Queen checkmate
desc: Push the king to the edge with your queen a knight's move away, bring your king up, then mate. Don't stalemate!

name: Rook checkmate
desc: Use the rook to cut the king off, shrink the box, and use your king to take away squares.

name: Two rooks: the ladder
desc: The rooks take turns checking and cutting off a rank - walk the king to the edge like a ladder.

name: Two bishops checkmate
desc: Bishops side by side make a wall. Drive the king to a corner with king support.

name: King in front of the pawn
desc: King on the 6th in front of its pawn always wins (except a rook pawn). Keep the opposition.

name: Rule of the square
desc: Can the king catch the pawn? Count the square - then just run.

name: Pawn breakthrough
desc: Three pawns against three: one of yours can break through with a sacrifice. Find b6!

name: Queen vs pawn on the 7th
desc: Check, then pin or force the king in front of its own pawn, and bring your king closer each time.

name: The Lucena position
desc: Build a bridge: Rook to the 4th rank, then walk your king out and block the checks with the rook.

name: Philidor defence
desc: Rook to your 3rd rank (...Ra6) to stop the king, and when the pawn advances, check from behind.

name: The wrong bishop
desc: The bishop can't control h8 - stay in the corner and it's a draw. Watch out for stalemate tricks on your side? No - just don't leave!

name: Take the opposition
desc: Face the king with one square between you. Keep the opposition and the pawn can't queen.

name: Rook vs bishop
desc: Usually a draw. Keep your king near the centre or in the corner of the OPPOSITE colour to your bishop.

name: Rook vs knight
desc: Keep the knight close to your king - a lone knight far away gets trapped.

name: Greek gift sacrifice
desc: Bxh7+! then Ng5+ and Qh5 - the classic sacrifice against a castled king.

name: Smothered mate
desc: Knight check, double check, queen sacrifice on g8, then the knight mates. Philidor's legacy.

name: Queen vs rook
desc: Push the king back, then win the rook with a fork or a skewer.

name: Rook vs minor + pawns
desc: You're the exchange up. Activate the rook, use the back rank and go after the pawns.

name: Two pieces vs rook
desc: Two minor pieces vs a rook: coordinate them and don't let the rook pick off a loose piece.

name: Queen vs two rooks
desc: Two rooks are strong when they work together - keep checking and look for forks.

name: Extra exchange
desc: Rook against bishop with pawns: use your king, attack pawns the bishop can't protect.

name: Piece vs three pawns
desc: The knight must blockade the pawns while your king comes over. Don't let them roll.

name: Two rooks vs queen
desc: Double your rooks, protect each other and your back rank - the queen can't do it alone.

name: Survive the Fried Liver
desc: Your king is on e6! Defend d5 with ...Ncb4 or ...Ne7 and bring your king to safety.
